description: A Long Term Support release, even-numbered and supported for at least three years, such as .NET 10 until 2028-11-14.
A Standard Term Support release, odd-numbered and supported for 24 months since .NET 9, such as .NET 9 and the upcoming .NET 11.
The TFM in the project file, such as net10.0 or netstandard2.0, which selects the available APIs and the default C# version.
A framework-dependent app automatically runs on the newest installed patch of its major version, but never moves to a new major version by itself.
A file at the repository root that pins which SDK version the dotnet CLI uses, with a rollForward policy for acceptable newer versions.
The date after which Microsoft ships no more fixes, including security fixes, for a .NET version.
The original Windows-only .NET, versions 4.x with C# 7.3 by default, which follows a separate lifecycle and is not the same product as modern .NET.
